scenes.heading: Terminating and recurring decimals
scenes.sub: Why do some decimals go on forever?
scenes.say: Three eighths is zero point three seven five. It stops. But two thirds is zero point six six six, forever! Why? Let's find out.
scenes.caption: 3/8 is 0.375. It stops. But 2/3 is 0.666…, forever! Why? Let's find out.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 3 pizzas for 8 people: each gets exactly 0.375
scenes.science: 2 pizzas for 3 people: there's always a bit left over
scenes.breaks: real pizza can't be cut forever, but in maths the division really never ends.
scenes.say: Share three pizzas between eight people. Everyone gets exactly zero point three seven five of a pizza, and you're done. Share two pizzas between three people and there's always a little bit left to cut. The analogy breaks down because real pizza can't be cut forever, but in maths the division never ends.
scenes.caption: Share 3 pizzas between 8 people. Everyone gets exactly 0.375 of a pizza, and you're done. Share 2 pizzas between 3 people and there's always a bit left to cut. The analogy breaks down because real pizza can't be cut forever, but in maths the division never ends.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of decimals
scenes.say: A terminating decimal stops, because the remainder reaches zero. A recurring decimal repeats forever, because a remainder comes back and the same digits come out again. Five elevenths is zero point four five four five, and so on.
scenes.caption: A terminating decimal stops, because the remainder reaches 0. A recurring decimal repeats forever, because a remainder comes back and the same digits come out again. 5/11 = 0.4545…

scenes.heading: Dot notation
points: Dot the first and last repeating digit
scenes.say: Instead of writing dot dot dot, put a dot over the repeating part. One repeating digit gets one dot. A repeating group gets a dot over its first and last digits. And only dot the digits that repeat: in one sixth, only the six repeats.

scenes.heading: Example
scenes.question: Write 5/11 as a decimal.
scenes.say: Write five elevenths as a decimal. Fifty divided by eleven is four, remainder six. Sixty divided by eleven is five, remainder five. Then fifty again! The digits repeat, so it's zero point four five, recurring, with dots on the four and the five.
scenes.caption: Write 5/11 as a decimal. 50 ÷ 11 = 4 r 6. 60 ÷ 11 = 5 r 5. Then 50 again! The digits repeat, so it's 0.4̇5̇, with dots on the 4 and the 5.

scenes.heading: Will it terminate?
scenes.say: Want to know before you divide? Simplify the fraction first. Then break the denominator into primes. If it has only twos and fives, it terminates. Any other prime, like three or seven, and it recurs.

Quick recap. A fraction is the top divided by the bottom. Terminating decimals stop; recurring ones repeat forever, and dots show the repeating part. Simplify first, then remember: only twos and fives get to stop. Now try the practice questions!
